From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: senorita and Señorita

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • senorita

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish señorita. Doublet of senhorita.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Anglicised) IPA(key): /sɛn.jəˈɹiː.tə/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iːtə

Noun

[edit]

señorita (plural señoritas)

  1. A young, unmarried woman in or from a Hispanophone community.
    I love it when you call me señorita.
  2. A small species of wrasse, Oxyjulis californica.
    • 1991, Martha Holmes, Sea Trek, BBC Books, page 79:
      The golden, cigar-shaped señoritas occur in schools that number from just a few fish to many hundreds.

Translations

[edit]
courtesy title for an unmarried woman in a Hispanophone country
  • Estonian: senjoriita
  • Japanese: セニョリータ (senyoriita)
  • Russian: сеньори́та (ru) f (senʹoríta)
  • Spanish: señorita (es) f

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Reitanos, Restaino, airstone, arsonite, asterion, notaries, notarise, rai stone, tonaries

Spanish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • Señorita (used before a name)
  • Srta., Srta (abbreviation)

Etymology

[edit]

From señora +‎ -ita.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /seɲoˈɾita/ [se.ɲoˈɾi.t̪a]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ita
  • Syllabification: se‧ño‧ri‧ta

Noun

[edit]

señorita f (plural señoritas, masculine señorito, masculine plural señoritos)

  1. young woman
    Colombia es conocida por sus bonitas señoritas. ― Colombia has a reputation for its pretty young women
  2. Miss (used as a title)
  3. (female) snob

Related terms

[edit]
  • seño
  • señorito

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Cebuano: senyorita
  • → Tagalog: senyorita

Further reading

[edit]
  • “señorito”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
